docs.title: What We Build
docs.text:
Artificial Brain Studio is our flagship platform for designing, training, and inspecting next-generation neural architectures. Instead of one fixed sequential network, builders create adaptive systems that grow internally and externally. Developers control where data enters, where outputs are produced, how modules communicate, where losses are applied, and how information flows, all within one visual and programmable environment.

During inference, the full internal data flow is observable. This makes AI decisions transparent, explainable, and controllable in a way that post-hoc methods cannot match.

docs.title: Scientific Foundation
docs.text:
Our technology is grounded in the Pursuit of Subspaces (PoS) hypothesis, an axiomatic mathematical framework that models neural reasoning as structured transformations between compact representation spaces. PoS provides a unified foundation for:

  • Explainability by design: transparency is structural, not approximate
  • Zero-shot and few-shot reasoning: generalisation from geometric properties alone
  • Adaptive neural computation: dynamic routing based on input geometry
  • Geometric counterfactual explanations: translating anomalous inputs toward normal representations
  • Privacy-preserving transformation: removing sensitive attributes while preserving task structure
  • Controllable human-AI alignment: steering behaviour through explicit geometric constraints

docs.title: Why Geometric AI?
docs.text:
Geometric AI is not just another AI model. It is a platform for building controllable, artificial brain-like systems where the internal flow of information is visible, measurable, redirectable, and human-supervisable.

Our long-term vision is two-fold:

Scientifically, we aim to build a mathematical foundation for understanding intelligence and, eventually, consciousness.

Commercially, we aim to build artificial brain systems that can reason, adapt, make analogies, and remain fully observable and controllable by humans.

docs.title: Artificial Brain Studio
docs.text:
Artificial Brain Studio is a visual and programmable platform for building next-generation neural architectures using modular Geometric AI components. Instead of designing one fixed sequential network, builders can create adaptive neural systems that grow internally and externally.

Developers can define where data enters, where outputs are produced, how modules communicate, where losses are applied, and how information flows through the system, without being locked into a single fixed architecture. The platform supports both research experimentation and production deployment.

During TrainingDuring Inference
  • Define data entry and output points for each modality
  • Activate or deactivate individual internal modules
  • Place loss functions between any two points in the network
  • Apply geometric transformations between modules
  • Monitor full training logs, metrics, and experiments in real time
  • Observe the complete internal data flow for any input
  • Identify which modules contributed to a given decision
  • Track how reasoning evolved step by step through the network
  • Generate geometric counterfactual explanations for any output

docs.title: Explainable Neural Architecture
docs.text: The system shows which modules contributed to a decision, which parts remained inactive, and how reasoning evolved internally. Transparency is built into the architecture, not bolted on as a post-hoc approximation.

docs.title: Adaptive On-the-Fly Reasoning
docs.text: Unlike frozen neural networks, Geometric AI systems can adapt internal pathways and representations during reasoning, potentially even from a single new sample. This enables genuine on-the-fly adaptation without retraining.

docs.title: Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
docs.text: The system learns what normal behaviour looks like and detects rare or abnormal events without requiring labelled failure examples. The decision boundary is defined geometrically from normal data alone.

docs.title: Geometric Counterfactual Explanation
docs.text: An abnormal input can be translated toward a normal or healthy representation, showing exactly what makes the input anomalous and what would need to change for it to be considered normal.

docs.title: Privacy-Preserving Transformation
docs.text: Sensitive, identity-specific information can be transformed while preserving the task-relevant structure of the representation. The transformed data remains useful for downstream inference without exposing the original sensitive content.

docs.title: Multimodal and Missing-Data Reasoning
docs.text: The system can reason across multiple data sources and update its decisions as new information arrives. Modules that receive no input remain inactive, so the system degrades gracefully when data is partial or missing.

docs.title: Energy-Efficient Adaptive Computation
docs.text: Only the necessary submodules are activated for a given input, enabling efficient deployment on edge devices and low-resource systems. Simple inputs follow short paths; ambiguous inputs engage more of the network.

docs.title: Pursuit of Subspaces (PoS)
docs.text:
Pursuit of Subspaces (PoS) is the scientific foundation of Geometric AI, an axiomatic mathematical framework that models neural networks as structured geometric systems. Drawing from the principles of Euclidean geometry, PoS formulates network behaviour through four geometric postulates, providing a unified explanation for representation, computation, and generalisation across architectures.

Within this framework, each layer or module acts as a geometric operator projecting information into progressively refined subspaces. Reasoning becomes traceable, explainability is structural rather than approximate, and capabilities such as zero-shot generalisation, counterfactual explanation, and privacy-preserving transformation emerge naturally from the formulation.

docs.title: Research Areas
docs.text:
The PoS framework underpins research across six interconnected directions:

  • Explainability by design: neural architectures whose internal structure makes decisions interpretable without approximation
  • Zero-shot and few-shot reasoning: generalisation to new classes and domains from geometric properties alone
  • Adaptive neural computation: dynamic routing through submodule chains based on input geometry
  • Geometric counterfactual explanations: minimum-distance transformations from anomalous to normal representations
  • Privacy-preserving transformation: orthogonal projection to remove sensitive attributes while preserving task structure
  • Controllable human-AI alignment: steering model behaviour through explicit geometric constraints rather than RLHF
